body.statement: For \(\mathfrak E_\star\) with uniform \(q\), \(F_{\mathcal J}=107/72\) and \(F_{\mathcal J,2}=F_{\mathcal J,3}=55/36\), so the exact gap is \(1/24\). By the strict class-inclusion proposition, every quadratic candidate allowed by the published Harshaw--Middleton--Savje framework lies in the Boolean comparison class \(\mathcal C_{\mathcal J}(f)\cap\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,2}\subseteq\mathcal C_{\mathcal J}(f)\cap\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,3}\); hence the same \(55/36\) lower certificate rules out every such published candidate, although it does not assert that \(55/36\) is the optimum of their smaller positive-semidefinite class. The displayed bounds satisfy \(r^\star(\theta)-b^\star(\theta)=[1+x_0x_1x_2x_5]/24\in\{0,1/12\}\), and \(b^\star(\theta)=3^{-1}\sum_{z=1}^3h_z^\star(\theta|_{O_z})\) with every table entry in \([0,5]\). The distribution \(\mu^\star\) certifies \(107/72\), and \(\nu^\star\) certifies \(55/36\), by exact observable-margin equalities and complementary slackness across all sixty-four schedules.
body.justification: This exact nonnegative certificate proves that the published quadratic comparison class is globally incomplete even for a small legal binary experiment.
body.gap: \cite{HarshawMiddletonSavje2026} optimizes only quadratic forms, and \cite{Lu2019FactorialBinary} sharpens one factorial variance without an arbitrary-design degree separation; neither contains this quartic witness or the \(1/24\) rational gap.
body.consumer: It gives a reproducible test instance for variance-bound software and a concrete design where a higher-order rule pointwise improves a best observable quadratic rule.
body.proof_tex:
All calculations below are over \(\mathbb Q\).  The three score vectors in \(\mathfrak E_\star\) are supported on their displayed observation sets, and their coordinate sums are zero.  Direct substitution in \(\text{def:score-variance}\) gives
\[
 c=(-2/3,-1,2/3,0,-1/3,4/3)
\]
and
\[
 9A=\begin{pmatrix}
 8&0&-8&0&-2&2\\
 0&6&0&6&-3&-9\\
 -8&0&8&0&2&-2\\
 0&6&0&6&-3&-9\\
 -2&-3&2&-3&2&4\\
 2&-9&-2&-9&4&14
 \end{pmatrix}. \tag{15}
\]
The observable complex consists of the empty set, six singletons, the nine pairs
\[
 01,02,05,12,13,15,25,34,35,
\]
the five triples \(012,015,025,125,135\), and the quartet \(0125\).  Here a digit string denotes its set of coordinate indices.

Expanding the displayed formula for \(b^\star\), or equivalently applying Boolean inversion to the three displayed tables, gives precisely the following nonzero coefficients:
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrrrr}
S&0&1&2&3&4&5&02&12&13\\ \hline
\beta_S&8/9&2/3&11/9&2/3&1/3&7/3&-19/9&-1/3&4/3
\end{array}
\]
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrrrr}
S&15&25&34&35&012&015&025&125&0125\\ \hline
\beta_S&-8/3&-1/3&-2/3&-2&1/3&1/3&1/3&1/3&-2/3.
\end{array} \tag{16}
\]
Thus \(b^\star\in\mathcal E_{\mathcal J}\), and the nonzero coefficient \(\beta_{0125}=-2/3\), together with uniqueness of Boolean inversion, proves \(b^\star\notin\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,3}\).  The polynomial \(r^\star\) contains only the constant and the nine displayed observable pairs in centered coordinates, hence \(r^\star\in\mathcal E_{\mathcal J,2}\).

We next certify feasibility on every schedule.  Order \(\Theta\) lexicographically as \(000000,000001,\ldots,111111\).  Substitution of (15) and the formula for \(b^\star\) gives the complete exact slack vector, arranged in rows of eight,
\[
72\{b^\star-f\}=\begin{array}{rrrrrrrr}
0&56&8&0&0&56&8&0\\
24&88&0&0&24&88&0&0\\
0&8&56&0&0&8&56&0\\
0&40&24&0&0&40&24&0\\
0&24&40&0&0&24&40&0\\
0&56&8&0&0&56&8&0\\
0&0&88&24&0&0&88&24\\
0&8&56&0&0&8&56&0
\end{array}. \tag{17}
\]
Every entry is nonnegative, so \(b^\star\ge f\).  If \(w=x_0x_1x_2x_5\in\{-1,1\}\), direct subtraction gives
\[
 r^\star(\theta)-b^\star(\theta)
 =\frac{110-107+3w}{72}=\frac{1+w}{24}\in\{0,1/12\}. \tag{18}
\]
Thus \(r^\star\ge b^\star\ge f\).  Uniform \(q\) has zero expectation for every nonconstant centered monomial, so
\[
 \mathbb E_qb^\star=\frac{107}{72},\quad\quad
 \mathbb E_qr^\star=\frac{110}{72}=\frac{55}{36}. \tag{19}
\]

The assignment-level equality is also exact.  With the coordinates in each \(O_z\) ordered as in \(\text{def:witness-experiment}\), let \(\iota_z(\theta)\) be the binary integer represented by \(\theta|_{O_z}\).  Substitution of the three rational tables gives
\[
 72\left\{\frac13\sum_{z=1}^3h_z^\star(\theta|_{O_z})
              -b^\star(\theta)\right\}=0
 \quad\text{for each of the sixty-four lexicographically ordered schedules}. \tag{20}
\]
Equivalently, Boolean inversion of the left side of (20) gives exactly the common coefficient list (16), which proves (20) without numerical tolerance.  Inspection of the displayed table entries gives
\[
 0\le h_z^\star(y)\le5\quad\quad(z=1,2,3; y\in\{0,1\}^{O_z}). \tag{21}
\]

For the all-degree lower certificate, each of the eight \(O_1\)-patterns occurs twice under the sixteen-point support of \(\mu^\star\), each of the four \(O_2\)-patterns occurs four times, and each of the sixteen \(O_3\)-patterns occurs once.  Hence \(\mu^\star\) has the uniform \(q\)-margin on every observed set and belongs to \(\mathcal D_{\mathcal J}(q)\).  The values of \(f\) on its support, in the order of \(\text{def:witness-experiment}\), are
\[
0,\frac23,\frac{32}{9},\frac{14}{9},\frac23,\frac83,
\frac{32}{9},\frac89,\frac89,\frac{14}{9},\frac83,\frac23,
\frac{14}{9},\frac{14}{9},\frac23,\frac23.
\]
Their mean is \(107/72\).  Direct lookup in (17) gives zero slack at all sixteen support points, so complementary slackness also holds.  The dual theorem and (19) now yield
\[
 F_{\mathcal J}=107/72. \tag{22}
\]

For the degree-three program, the eight-point support of \(\nu^\star\) contains each \(O_1\)-pattern once and each \(O_2\)-pattern twice.  Its \(O_3\)-projections are exactly the eight odd-parity four-bit strings, once each.  Therefore every proper-subset marginal of \(O_3\) is uniform: after fixing at most three bits, exactly \(2^{3-|S|}\) odd-parity completions remain.  These facts match the uniform \(q\)-moment of every observable monomial of degree at most three.  The corresponding variance values are
\[
\frac83,\frac{14}{9},\frac23,\frac89,
\frac{14}{9},\frac23,\frac{14}{9},\frac83,
\]
whose mean is \(55/36\); direct substitution gives \(r^\star=f\) at all eight support points.  Weak duality for the degree-three restriction and feasibility of \(r^\star\) give
\[
 \frac{55}{36}\le F_{\mathcal J,3}\le F_{\mathcal J,2}\le\frac{55}{36}. \tag{23}
\]
Thus both restricted values equal \(55/36\).  The dual fails only at the observable quartet: \(\mathbb E_{\nu^\star}m_{0125}=0\), whereas \(\mathbb E_qm_{0125}=1/16\); equivalently, \(\mathbb E_{\nu^\star}x_0x_1x_2x_5=-1\) and the uniform expectation is zero.  Equations (22)--(23) give
\[
 \frac{55}{36}-\frac{107}{72}=\frac{3}{72}=\frac1{24}. \tag{24}
\]
Finally, every coordinate in this witness is observed with positive probability, so the corrected \(\text{prop:hms-class-inclusion}\) applies to every compatible conservative Harshaw--Middleton--Savje quadratic candidate.  Such a candidate lies in the degree-two Boolean feasible class and therefore has uniform objective at least \(55/36\) by (23).  This lower bound is for the enlarged Boolean class and does not assert attainment within the smaller positive-semidefinite class.
